technical_and_design_decisions: Work on the Spring XD 1.1.0.RELEASE code base with its existing Gradle-based build; no application code changes are required, only benchmarking, documentation, and build/publishing work.
Use the RabbitMQ PerfTest load-generation tool to drive RabbitMQ throughput/latency benchmarks in a topology representative of an XD cluster (single node and clustered configurations).
Use Kafka's built-in performance utilities (kafka-producer-perf-test.sh and kafka-consumer-perf-test.sh) as required by U5, with no custom benchmark tooling development.

Reproduce the LinkedIn reference topology for U5: 3 Kafka brokers on separate EC2 instances, a 3-node ZooKeeper ensemble, replication factor 3, and 6 producer instances, targeting the published ~2M writes/sec baseline.
Publish RPMs to repo.spring.io (libs-release-local) using the existing Gradle Artifactory publishing configuration extended with the spring.io repository target and credentials.
Deliver module descriptions in two forms: concise high-level javadoc at the module definition level (U2) and expanded user-facing descriptions in the reference documentation/wiki (U4).
Deliver the message header change documentation (U6) as a new section in the existing GitHub wiki Deployment troubleshooting page.
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; estimates are effort (workdays), not elapsed calendar time.
The Spring XD 1.1.0 source tree, build environment, and commit/wiki access are available from day one.
An AWS account with permissions and credentials to create EC2 instances is available; EC2 monetary cost is out of scope.
Spring XD 1.1.0 ships roughly 50 modules (sources, sinks, processors, jobs) that each need a brief high-level description; U4 descriptions are short extensions of the U2 javadoc content.
The Gradle build already produces RPM artifacts; only publishing to repo.spring.io and verification of the published bits are needed for U3.
Kafka version is the one bundled/validated with Spring XD 1.1 (0.8.x line); RabbitMQ version is the version supported by XD 1.1 (3.3.x line).
Benchmark runs include warm-up and repeat executions; wall-clock run time overlaps with light monitoring effort and is charged at monitoring effort, not full hands-on effort.
Existing 1.0 batch-jobs and the documented message header deltas between 1.0 and 1.1 are available as input for U6.

activities.activity_description: Review all user stories, confirm scope per story, set up local build of Spring XD 1.1.0, and prepare workstation/tooling (Gradle build, benchmark clients, wiki access).
Provision and configure RabbitMQ nodes and the PerfTest client environment, including clustered configuration representative of an XD deployment.
Run throughput and latency benchmark scenarios (varying producers, consumers, message sizes, durability) using PerfTest.

activities.activity_name: RabbitMQ results analysis and reference report (U1)
activities.activity_description: Consolidate benchmark results into a reference report usable for sizing an XD cluster and publish it to the wiki.
Write concise high-level descriptions for each module (~50 modules) in the module definition javadoc and verify generated output.
Expand the module javadoc content into user-facing descriptions of purpose and capabilities in the reference documentation/wiki.
Extend the Gradle/Artifactory publishing configuration to publish Spring XD RPMs to repo.spring.io libs-release-local, including credentials handling and staging.
Publish the 1.1.0.RELEASE RPMs, then download them from repo.spring.io and verify installability and integrity.

activities.activity_name: EC2 infrastructure research for Kafka perf tests (U7)
activities.activity_description: Research and document the EC2 instance types, counts, storage, and network placement needed to reproduce the LinkedIn 'three cheap machines' benchmark topology.
Identify and document broker, topic, replication, and OS/JVM tuning configurations required for the performance test setup.

activities.activity_name: Provisioning of Kafka/ZooKeeper cluster on EC2 (U5/U7/U8)
activities.activity_description: Create EC2 instances, install and configure a 3-node ZooKeeper ensemble and 3 Kafka brokers per the identified configuration, and smoke-test the cluster.
Run the built-in producer and consumer perf utilities across the benchmark matrix (message sizes, batch sizes, producer counts, replication, async/sync), including warm-up and repeat runs.

activities.activity_name: Kafka results analysis vs LinkedIn baseline (U5)
activities.activity_description: Analyze collected metrics, compare against the LinkedIn engineering baseline (~2M writes/sec), explain deviations, and write the benchmark report as the foundation for XD use-cases.
Document the 1.0-to-1.1 message header changes, serialization error symptoms, and remediation steps in the wiki Deployment troubleshooting section.
